hypothesis: The current pair loop calculates j = k + (k >= i) for every interaction. Iterating directly over the two source ranges on either side of i should remove that per-pair comparison and index correction while visiting particles in the same order and leaving the floating-point arithmetic unchanged. The split loops may add divergence or code-size cost, so the controller must measure the official geometric-mean objective.
notes: This candidate changes only source indexing and preserves the existing force/acceleration arithmetic, rsqrtf formulation, mass handling, and ascending order of contributing particles. Earlier attempts h01 and h02 failed protected correctness at n=16384 with max absolute error 0.0003108978271484375; this candidate avoids further numerical reformulation. The valid baseline measured mean_seconds 0.0018473421059835202, but no per-size timings or candidate measurements are available here.
transformations: Replace the fixed k loop and per-interaction conditional source-index adjustment with two direct ranges, j < i and j > i.
Preserve the original ascending source visit order and per-pair floating-point expressions.
